radii.source: radii: NAIF pck00011.tpc (IAU WGCCRE 2015); mean radius: JPL planetary/satellite physical parameters

calibration.ref: NSSDC geometric albedo 1.0, capped at 0.9 to keep detail in 8-bit sRGB

landmarks.name: Ali Baba crater
landmarks.ref: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, feature 184 (56.84 N, 17.51 W, 34 km), the largest named crater; the mosaic is high-pass filtered, so craters show as shading

landmarks.name: Dunyazad crater
landmarks.ref: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, feature 1669 Dunyazad (41.51 N, 202.04 W = 157.96 E, 30.8 km), in the cratered plains of the leading side; this bake: texture ratio 1.32, mirrored 0.93 (smooth terrain), shifted 0.91

landmarks.name: Zumurrud crater
landmarks.ref: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, feature 14242 Zumurrud (22.23 S, 182.05 W = 177.95 E, 20.8 km); this bake: texture ratio 1.71, mirrored 0.85, shifted 0.85

landmarks.name: Long axis toward Saturn
landmarks.ref: IAU WGCCRE radii (pck00011): a = 256.6 km along the prime meridian, mean 252.1 km, so the surface at 0 N 0 E lies about +4.5 km above the mean sphere (local relief +-1 km); the shape model reads +4.9 km (a 90-degree error would read near -0.7 km, the b axis)

landmarks.name: Basin north of Sarandib Planitia
landmarks.ref: the deepest of the ~100-km basins in this shape model (Bland et al. 2020), centred at 24.8 N 45.8 E, about 60 km north of IAU Gazetteer feature 5323 Sarandib Planitia (10.23 N, 311.82 W = 48.18 E, 165 km); Schenk and McKinnon (2009, GRL 36, L16202) describe 90-175 km basins 0.8-1.5 km deep on Enceladus. Located from this DEM, so it checks the bake's handling of the DEM; the Gazetteer albedo landmarks and the long axis check the registration. This bake: 0.86 km, mirrored 0.05, shifted -0.09
